minutes.headline: Commissioners debated voicing personal views on the SRF treatment-plant funding article before next week's town vote.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners reviewed PFAS/PFOA testing changes and the SRF-funded treatment plant project ahead of a special town meeting vote on the funding article, agreeing commissioners could state individual opinions rather than a board position. The board also heard the superintendent's report on leak repairs and new radio equipment, discussed a manganese corrective action plan, and set homework for members to bring documentation on Zone I violations at the Hickory Hills well site for a decision at the next meeting. A commissioner separately raised concerns about the board's informal handling of motions and action items, prompting agreement to be more formal going forward.

what_happened.line: Commissioners agreed individual members may state personal views on the SRF treatment-plant funding article ahead of next week's town vote, rather than adopting a board position.
The board set homework: members are to bring documentation on Zone I violations at the Hickory Hills well site so a decision can be made at the June 10 meeting.
No money will be spent on the Zone I violation issue until the board meets again and works out a plan.
A commissioner raised concerns about the board's informal handling of motions, and the board agreed to formalize agreements as motions and action items going forward.
The superintendent reported on water main leak repairs and new radio/antenna equipment, and the board discussed a manganese corrective action plan for the Lancaster wells.

why_it_matters: The SRF-funded treatment plant article goes to a special town meeting vote requiring two-thirds approval, and it touches how the district's largest current capital project gets paid for.
Zone I protections at the Hickory Hills well concern the buffer around a water supply source; the board is holding off on spending until it decides its approach at the next meeting.
Moving from informal consensus to formal motions changes how a resident can later verify what the board actually decided and when.
